Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked. this is only one component so in one file at all



Reasoning accordion (cot-message-chunk, cot-v5) featuring live step spinners, progress checkmarks, and dynamic height transitions.
use liquid glass
Rather than blurring whatever sits behind it, a Liquid Glass surface bends that content the way a real lens would, catches specular highlights that shift as you tilt the device, and adapts its own tint and shadow to whatever is passing underneath. Move the content, and the glass responds. It is closer to a simulated physical object than to a CSS effect.
The distinction that matters: glassmorphism blurs what is behind it, Liquid Glass refracts it. Add specular highlights that track device motion, tint and shadow that respond to the content passing underneath, and shapes that morph and merge into one another as the interface changes, and you have a material that is simulated per frame rather than declared once.

Practically: most of what gets posted online as “liquid glass” on the web is glassmorphism with better lighting. Genuine refraction in a browser needs displacement mapping or a shader, not backdrop-filter

többrétegű valós idejű fénytörő kompozíciós anyagrendszert UI elemekhez Apple platformokra. A komponensnek meg kell valósítania az adaptív áttetszőséget, az optikai fénytörést, a spekuláris kiemeléseket, a kromatikus effektusokat, a fénysűrűség-vezérelt színezést és a folyamatos sima alakzat-összeolvadást
Kezdd a mag réteg-hierarchia meghatározásával, amelyet minden üveg-elem futásidőben felépít:
•  Egy gyökér konténer réteg, amely a teljes effektus-vermet fogadja.
•  Egy opcionális magasabb szintű burkoló réteg, amely több elem-példányt kezel.
•  Egy elsődleges mintavételező réteg CABackdropLayer típusból, amely a WindowServer útvonalon keresztül rögzíti az elem mögötti tartalmat. Bővítsd ki ezt a réteget a következő tulajdonságokkal: tracksLuma (logikai érték, amely vezérli, hogy a réteg folyamatosan mintavételezi-e az alatta lévő fénysűrűséget), lumaSubrect (CGRect, amely a fénysűrűség-követéshez használt régiót határozza meg), allowsFilteredLuma (logikai érték, amely lehetővé teszi fekete vagy fehér átfedő réteg beállítását), és lumaUpdateRate (lebegőpontos érték, amely a fénysűrűség-frissítések időbeli simítását vezérli). Konfiguráld a réteget úgy, hogy window-server tudatos maradjon, és egyedi csoportnevet használjon a helyes kompozíciós elkülönítéshez.
•  A mintavételező rétegen belül egy SDF textúra-forrás réteg CASDFLayer típusból, amely az “@0” névvel van azonosítva. Ennek a rétegnek generálnia kell a tartalmazott geometria signed-distance-field ábrázolását és a megfelelő normáltérképet.
•  Az SDF textúra-forrás rétegen belül egy egyszerű CALayer konténer, amely egy vagy több CASDFElementLayer példányt tartalmaz. Minden CASDFElementLayer egyetlen alakzat geometriai leírását tárolja signed distance field formájában.
•  Két további testvér CASDFLayer példány az “@1” és “@2” nevekkel. Ezek a rétegek irányított üveg-kiemelés effektusokat kapnak, és mindegyik tartalmaz egy SDFPortalLayer-t, amely a primer CASDFElementLayer geometriáját tükrözi teljes újraraszterizálás nélkül.
•  Alkalmazz egy “glassBackground” nevű CAFilter-t az elsődleges CABackdropLayer-re. A szűrőnek az SDF normáltérkép textúrát az inputSourceSublayerName kulcson keresztül kell fogadnia, amely “@0”-ra van állítva, és végre kell hajtania a fénytörést, a Gauss-elmosódást, a vibrancy-beállítást, a tónusleképezést és a kromatikus diszperziót. További vibrantColorMatrix típusú szűrők alkalmazhatók a kiemelés-rétegekre színmátrix-tónusvezérléshez.
Valósítsd meg a következő privát-effektus osztályokat, amelyek az SDF feldolgozást konfigurálják:
•  CASDFOutputEffect, amely az alakzat-rétegeket backdrop-kompatibilis SDF textúrákká alakítja.
•  CASDFGlassHighlightEffect, amely irányfüggő élvilágítást generál a felületi normálok és egy konfigurálható fényirány alapján.
•  CASDFGlassDisplacementEffect, amely a fénytörési eltolás mértékét és lecsengését vezérli.
Minden SDF geometriát signed-distance függvényekkel kell definiálni. Biztosíts analitikus SDF primitíveket lekerekített téglalapokhoz (szuperellipszis támogatás opcionális), és valósíts meg egy sima-unió operátort, amely két SDF értéket és egy k keverési együtthatót fogad, folyamatos, paramétervezérelt alakzat-összeolvadást eredményezve. Vezesd le a felületi normálokat a kombinált SDF analitikus vagy véges-különbséges gradienseiből; ezek a normálok vezérlik mind a fénytörést, mind a spekuláris kiemelés-számításokat.
árnyékoló is kell, amely végrehajtja az optikai szimulációt. A fragment shadernek:
•  Mintavételeznie kell a CABackdropLayer-től kapott háttértextúrát.
•  Ki kell számítania a helyi SDF értéket és annak gradiensét minden fragmentumnál.
•  Ki kell számítania a fénytörési eltolásokat a Metal refract függvény használatával, független törésmutatókat támogatva a vörös, zöld és kék csatornákhoz a kromatikus aberráció előállításához.
•  Alkalmaznia kell Fresnel-stílusú élintenzitást a nézési szög koszinusza alapján.
•  Generálnia kell irányított spekuláris kiemeléseket, amelyek a felületi normálokra és egy dinamikus fényirányra reagálnak.
•  Végre kell hajtania mip-leképezett elmosódást, amelynek sugara az SDF felszínhez mért távolsága szerint modulálódik.
•  Be kell építenie az adaptív színezést a követett fénysűrűség-értékekből.
•  Ki kell adnia a végső színt helyes előszorzott alfával.
A rendszernek automatikusan adaptálnia kell az átlátszatlanságot, az elmosódás sugarát és a fénysűrűség-követés erősségét az elem mérete és az alatta lévő tartalom fénysűrűsége szerint. A nagyobb elemek erősebb szóródást és mélyebb árnyékokat kapnak; a görgetési él-régiók további elmosódást és átlátszatlanság-csökkentést kapnak az olvashatóság megőrzése érdekében. A teljes effektus-veremnek interaktív képkockasebességet kell fenntartania (cél 120 Hz a támogatott hardveren) az Apple GPU-k csempe-alapú késleltetett renderelési jellemzőinek és a nulla-másolású IOSurface útvonalaknak a kihasználásával, ahol lehetséges.

entries.answer:
Build a single-file, production-ready Apple-platform UI component that implements a reasoning accordion with expandable step-by-step message chunks, live activity spinners, completion checkmarks, animated progress state changes, and smoothly interpolated dynamic height transitions. The component must render the accordion and its optical material entirely through a real-time, multilayer refractive glass system rather than a conventional blurred-transparency effect. Do not use backdrop blurring as the primary visual mechanism. Treat the glass surface as a simulated optical object that refracts the live content behind it, responds to changes in underlying luminance and color, produces motion-responsive specular highlights, supports chromatic dispersion, and allows adjacent component surfaces to smoothly morph and visually merge.

Implement everything in one complete, unabridged source file. Include all required UI declarations, rendering infrastructure, layer composition, shader source, signed-distance-field geometry functions, animation control, luminance tracking, lifecycle handling, resource management, event handling, accessibility support, and state-update logic. Do not depend on unfinished APIs, placeholder methods, mock implementations, dummy data, simulated rendering paths, or external source files. The resulting file must compile and run as a complete production component on supported Apple platforms.

## Component behavior

Construct an accordion interface composed of one or more reasoning steps. Each step must support the following states:

- Collapsed: display a compact summary row with the step title, current status icon, and a disclosure control.
- Expanding: animate the disclosure state, content height, corner geometry, refractive material bounds, shadow shape, and SDF union parameters continuously.
- Active: display a live spinner while work is in progress, show the step content as it becomes available, and update progress affordances without interrupting the material animation.
- Completed: replace the spinner with an animated progress checkmark, preserve the final content, and smoothly settle the glass material into its completed visual state.
- Collapsing: reverse the layout, SDF geometry, highlight, displacement, opacity, shadow, and clipping animations without visual snapping.
- Error or interrupted: render a distinct status treatment while preserving readability, accessibility labels, and the same physical-material rendering model.

Render accordion rows and expanded content in a shared composition hierarchy so nearby glass elements can optically influence one another. When two adjacent accordion surfaces overlap, approach each other, expand, collapse, or are visually grouped, blend their signed-distance fields through a continuous smooth-union operation so their boundaries merge naturally rather than appearing as independent rounded rectangles.

Support interactive input through taps, clicks, keyboard activation, accessibility actions, and programmatic state changes. Respect reduced-motion settings by reducing or removing nonessential motion while preserving state visibility, layout correctness, disclosure semantics, and status changes. Keep live state updates stable while an expand or collapse animation is in progress; do not reset, recreate, or visually tear the refractive backing surface when message content changes.

## Core rendering hierarchy

Build the complete visual system at runtime using a root composition container and a hierarchy equivalent to the following structure:

1. Create a root container layer that owns the entire optical effect stack, clips and positions the rendered material correctly, and synchronizes its layout with the accordion’s visible bounds.

2. Add an optional higher-level wrapper layer capable of managing multiple component instances or multiple glass elements within the same composition group. Use this wrapper to coordinate z-order, shared material bounds, shared SDF composition, merging behavior, and group-level rendering updates.

3. Create a primary backdrop sampling layer based on `CABackdropLayer`. Configure it to capture the content visually behind each glass element through the WindowServer-backed compositing path. Keep the layer WindowServer-aware and assign a unique composition group name so backdrop sampling remains isolated from unrelated material surfaces.

4. Extend the primary backdrop sampling layer with the following runtime-configurable properties:

   - `tracksLuma: Bool`, controlling whether continuous underlying-luminance sampling is active.
   - `lumaSubrect: CGRect`, defining the local region used for luminance measurement.
   - `allowsFilteredLuma: Bool`, controlling whether black or white overlay treatment can be applied as part of luminance adaptation.
   - `lumaUpdateRate: CGFloat`, controlling temporal smoothing and update cadence for luminance values.

5. Inside the primary backdrop layer, create an SDF texture-source layer based on `CASDFLayer`, identified exactly as `"@0"`. Configure this layer to generate both a signed-distance-field representation and a corresponding normal-map representation of all contained geometry.

6. Inside the `"@0"` SDF layer, create a standard `CALayer` geometry container. Populate it with one or more `CASDFElementLayer` instances. Each element layer must define exactly one SDF-backed geometric shape corresponding to a visible accordion surface, header region, expanded content region, status-chip region, or merged visual grouping.

7. Add two sibling `CASDFLayer` instances identified exactly as `"@1"` and `"@2"`. Use these layers for directional glass-highlight generation. Each highlight layer must contain an `SDFPortalLayer` that references the geometry of the primary `CASDFElementLayer` content without forcing an independent full rasterization pass.

8. Apply a filter named `"glassBackground"` to the primary backdrop layer. Configure the filter’s `inputSourceSublayerName` to `"@0"` so the filter receives the SDF normal-map texture from the primary SDF source. The filter pipeline must execute optical refraction, mip-aware Gaussian blur, vibrancy adjustment, tone mapping, chromatic dispersion, luminance-responsive tinting, and premultiplied-alpha composition.

9. Apply additional `vibrantColorMatrix`-style filters to the `"@1"` and `"@2"` highlight layers where needed. Use these color-matrix filters to independently control warm and cool highlight balance, intensity, contrast, saturation, opacity, and directional edge treatment.

10. Ensure all layers update coherently during scrolling, resizing, rotation, safe-area changes, content updates, display-scale changes, dynamic-type changes, expansion transitions, and interactive gestures.

## SDF geometry system

Define every material shape through signed-distance functions. Do not use static raster masks as the main geometry representation. Generate SDF values at render time or maintain GPU-ready SDF textures whose contents are updated only when geometry changes.

Implement analytic SDF primitives for:

- Rounded rectangles with independently configurable width, height, radius, and corner behavior.
- Capsules for compact status chips and checkmark backgrounds.
- Circles for spinner geometry and circular indicators.
- Optional superellipse support for more fluid and less mechanically rounded contours.
- Arbitrary unions of component surfaces for grouped accordion material.
- Optional subtraction or intersection operations for cutouts, internal borders, or inset content regions.

Implement a smooth-union function that accepts two SDF values and a blend coefficient `k`, producing a continuous, parameter-controlled blended field. Use it to merge neighboring accordion panels, header and content surfaces during expansion, grouped content rows, and other intersecting material regions. The merging animation must be smooth in both geometry and derivative behavior so visual normals and highlights do not visibly pop.

Use the combined SDF field to determine:

- The inside/outside mask.
- The distance to the nearest material boundary.
- The local boundary softness.
- The blur modulation radius.
- The refractive displacement strength.
- The shadow falloff.
- The luminance-adaptation contribution.
- The Fresnel edge response.
- The optical highlight region.
- The local normal direction.

Derive normals from the SDF gradient. Use analytic gradients where practical and stable; otherwise use central finite differences with a sufficiently small texel- or display-scale-aware epsilon. Normalize the resulting gradient before use in refraction, Fresnel, directional lighting, and specular calculations.

## Optical material shader

Embed complete Metal shader source in the same file and compile it at runtime or package it through an in-file mechanism supported by the target language and platform. The rendering path must sample the real backdrop texture supplied by the compositing system and render the optical result in real time.

For every fragment, execute the following process:

1. Sample the background texture captured from the backdrop sampling layer or the associated zero-copy IOSurface-backed texture path.

2. Evaluate the local combined signed-distance value and calculate its gradient-derived surface normal.

3. Determine whether the fragment lies inside the glass material, at its boundary, or outside the material. Use anti-aliased SDF coverage for edge smoothness.

4. Construct an incident view vector and refract it against the SDF-derived normal using Metal’s `refract` function or an equivalent physically consistent implementation.

5. Support separate refractive indices or channel-specific displacement scales for red, green, and blue. Refract or offset each color channel independently to create controlled chromatic aberration while preventing visible color fringing from exceeding the material boundary.

6. Sample the backdrop texture using the red, green, and blue refracted coordinates. Combine the sampled channels into a chromatically dispersed refracted background color.

7. Apply mip-aware Gaussian blur. Select or interpolate mip levels according to the local blur radius, and modulate that radius by distance to the SDF surface, component size, scrolling-edge state, motion state, local backdrop contrast, and luminance conditions. Preserve fine detail near edges where optical definition is required and increase scattering deeper within larger surfaces.

8. Calculate a Fresnel-style edge response using the cosine of the view angle relative to the surface normal. Increase edge brightness and reflectance at grazing angles while maintaining a restrained response over the center of the surface.

9. Calculate directional specular highlights from the surface normal, a dynamically configurable light direction, view direction, roughness value, and a physically plausible or artistically controlled specular exponent. Make highlight direction and position respond continuously to device motion, pointer position, or other available interaction-driven lighting input.

10. Blend independently generated highlights from the `"@1"` and `"@2"` layers. Support at least two directional light treatments, such as a cool top-left light and a warm lower-right reflected light, with independently adjustable color matrices and intensities.

11. Track luminance in the `lumaSubrect` region when `tracksLuma` is enabled. Smooth luminance changes temporally according to `lumaUpdateRate`. Use the measured luminance to adapt glass tint, opacity, vibrancy, shadow density, contrast protection, and optional black or white overlay behavior when `allowsFilteredLuma` is enabled.

12. Adapt material opacity, blur radius, refraction displacement, shadow depth, and contrast treatment to element size. Larger accordion elements must receive stronger internal scattering, deeper shadows, and appropriately scaled optical distortion. Compact rows must remain legible and avoid excessive distortion.

13. Detect scroll-edge regions and apply additional blur plus controlled opacity reduction to maintain readable content as the accordion approaches clipping or scrolling boundaries.

14. Composite the final refracted background, tint, Fresnel response, highlights, shadow contribution, and anti-aliased SDF edge coverage using correct premultiplied alpha. Ensure output color and alpha remain valid for all layer opacity values, dark and bright backdrops, reduced-transparency settings, and animated transitions.

## Private effect abstractions

Implement the internal effect abstractions needed to configure the SDF and backdrop pipeline:

- `CASDFOutputEffect`: converts the SDF element-layer geometry into backdrop-compatible SDF and normal-map textures for use by the main glass filter.
- `CASDFGlassHighlightEffect`: generates direction-dependent edge lighting from surface normals and configurable light vectors.
- `CASDFGlassDisplacementEffect`: controls refractive displacement magnitude, falloff, channel separation, edge protection, and animation behavior.

Integrate these abstractions into the layer hierarchy, shader uniforms, and rendering scheduler. If the platform does not expose a needed implementation detail publicly, provide a production-safe rendering implementation using supported Metal, Core Animation, Core Graphics, and IOSurface-compatible mechanisms while preserving the same rendered behavior. Do not rely on undocumented runtime invocation, unstable private symbols, or unsupported binary interfaces.

## Animation and interaction

Use a display-synchronized rendering loop and transaction-based layer updates to maintain smooth, coherent animation. Target 120 Hz on supported displays while adapting frame pacing to device capability and thermal conditions.

Animate all of the following continuously and without layout jumps:

- Accordion content height.
- Header and content bounds.
- SDF primitive dimensions.
- Rounded-corner radius.
- Smooth-union coefficient.
- Refractive displacement strength.
- Blur radius.
- Highlight direction and intensity.
- Tint and luminance adaptation.
- Shadow depth and softness.
- Spinner rotation and progress state.
- Checkmark stroke drawing and completion scale.
- Disclosure indicator rotation.
- Layer opacity and material visibility.

Use interpolation curves appropriate to physical material transitions, including critically damped or spring-like motion where useful. Preserve deterministic final states. During interactive dragging, scrolling, and disclosure gestures, use continuous gesture progress to drive geometry and shader parameters directly rather than triggering only discrete animations.

Use zero-copy IOSurface or equivalent shared-texture paths where possible. Avoid unnecessary texture readback, CPU-side image processing, repeated full-screen rendering, or re-rasterization of unchanged SDF geometry. Exploit Apple GPU tile-based deferred rendering behavior by minimizing intermediate render targets, preserving tile-local operations where possible, batching compatible passes, and restricting redraws to dirty regions.

## Layout, accessibility, and reliability

Implement responsive layout for all supported device sizes, display scales, orientations, split-screen modes, safe-area insets, dynamic type sizes, and right-to-left layout direction. Recompute SDF geometry, texture dimensions, luminance regions, hit-testing regions, and shader uniforms whenever layout changes.

Expose a clear public API for:

- Creating accordion steps.
- Providing title and content.
- Updating live reasoning text.
- Setting step state and progress.
- Expanding or collapsing a specific step.
- Configuring light direction, refraction strength, blur intensity, chromatic dispersion, tint behavior, and luminance tracking.
- Enabling or disabling merged-material behavior.
- Receiving state-change callbacks.
- Controlling reduced-motion and reduced-transparency behavior.

Implement accessibility labels, traits, values, hints, focus order, keyboard navigation, disclosure actions, and live-region announcements for active and completed steps. Ensure that status changes are announced correctly and that the visual glass effect never becomes the sole carrier of semantic information.

Handle memory warnings, application backgrounding, foreground restoration, display-link pausing, texture recreation, backing-store changes, and view removal safely. Release GPU resources when the component is no longer visible and recreate only the resources required when rendering resumes.

Validate all geometry inputs, clamp shader parameters to stable ranges, prevent invalid texture coordinates, guard against zero-size layouts, avoid divide-by-zero in SDF and lighting calculations, and ensure all compositing paths preserve correct premultiplied-alpha behavior.
